title: Component dimensions after a field extension from local dimensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $L/k$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Form $Y_L=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ with projection $p:Y_L\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $Y_L$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and for every $w\in Y_L$ one has $\dim_w(Y_L)=\dim_{p(w)}Y$, where $\dim_w$ denotes local topological dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Every irreducible component $D$ of $Y_L$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] has a generic point $z$ [def-sc-generic-point], and for every such $z$ one has $\dim D=\dim_z(Y_L)=\dim_{p(z)}Y$, with $\dim$ denoting topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. In particular, if $d\in\mathbb N$ and $\dim_yY=d$ for every $y\in Y$, every irreducible component of $Y_L$ has dimension $d$. Empty $Y$ is permitted; no purity or irreducibility of $Y$ and no algebraicity or separability of $L/k$ is assumed.

proof.text: Let $q:Y_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ be the second projection. The locally-finite-type base-change lemma applies to $g$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $q$ is locally of finite type. The field $L$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $L$, generated respectively by $0$ and $1$. Thus the single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}L$ makes it locally Noetherian. Apply the locally-Noetherian-source lemma to $q$ to obtain that $Y_L$ is locally Noetherian. No finiteness assumption on $L/k$ occurs.

Fix $w\in Y_L$. Apply the fibre-dimension base-change lemma to the defining cartesian square for $Y_L$ and $g$. Its finite-type hypothesis is exactly the given local finite type of $g$. For the unique points $s\in\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $s\prime\in\operatorname{Spec}L$, the fibres $Y_s$ and $(Y_L)_{s\prime}$ identify respectively with $Y$ and $Y_L$: the residue fields are $k$ and $L$, and pulling back over either base along its identity gives the original scheme. The cited fibre definition identifies their topological spaces with the whole inverse images of these points. The local dimensions in the base-change lemma are the minima of dimensions of open neighbourhoods, as in the two cited dimension definitions. Consequently its equality reads $\dim_w(Y_L)=\dim_{p(w)}Y$.

source.place: Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), part (1), with S=Spec k and S\prime=Spec L.

proof.text: Let $D$ be an irreducible component of $Y_L$. A scheme is sober, so the scheme-sobriety lemma supplies a generic point $z$ of the closed irreducible subset $D$. This establishes the existence required in the statement.

For any generic point $z$ of $D$, one has $D=\overline{\{z\}}$. If another irreducible component $E$ contains $z$, its closedness implies $D\subseteq E$. Maximality of the irreducible subset $D$ then gives $D=E$. Therefore $D$ is the only component through $z$. Apply the locally-algebraic maximum formula to the locally finite type $L$-scheme $Y_L$ from step 1 at $z$. The maximum has the single value $\dim D$, so $\dim_z(Y_L)=\dim D$. Combining this with step 2 at $w=z$ gives $\dim D=\dim_z(Y_L)=\dim_{p(z)}Y$.

source.place: Tag 0B1B, first equality in item-dimension-irreducibles-passing-through of lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic.

proof.text: If $\dim_yY=d$ for every $y\in Y$, substitute $y=p(z)$ into step 4 to get $\dim D=d$ for each component $D$ of $Y_L$. If $Y$ is empty, its fibre product $Y_L$ is empty as well (its first projection has empty target), so there are no points or components to check.
